Name: nn_architecture_impact
Title: Neural Network Architecture Impact on Orbit Correction Accuracy
Experiment: Compare orbit correction performance (L₂ residual) of different neural network architectures (Dense, CNN, LSTM) trained on identical datasets. Evaluate sensitivity to hidden parameter variations and computational efficiency.

Name: data_scaling_effect
Title: Training Data Scaling Effects on ML Correction Robustness
Experiment: Quantify orbit correction improvement when increasing training samples (100→1000) and tightening optimization tolerance (1e-8→1e-10). Measure generalization to unseen σψ variations.

Name: hybrid_correction
Title: Hybrid SVD-Neural Network Correction Framework
Experiment: Develop cascade system: SVD coarse correction followed by NN residual optimization. Compare pure NN/SVD against hybrid approach in computational cost and orbit minimization.

Name: online_adaptation
Title: Online Adaptation of Neural Corrector via Transfer Learning
Experiment: Implement real-time NN fine-tuning using transfer learning when accelerator configuration drifts. Measure steps required to adapt to new σₓ/σᵧ regimes without full retraining.

Name: uncertainty_quantification
Title: Uncertainty Quantification in NN-Based Orbit Prediction
Experiment: Incorporate Monte Carlo dropout in neural network to estimate uncertainty bounds for corrector magnet settings. Validate against MAD-X perturbation analysis.

Name: ensemble_correction
Title: Ensemble Learning for Improved Orbit Correction
Experiment: Develop an ensemble correction framework combining SVD and neural network predictions. Implement a mechanism to blend outputs (e.g., weighted average or voting). Evaluate performance improvement in orbit minimization and robustness to hidden parameter variations compared to standalone methods.

Name: reinforcement_learning_orbit_control
Title: Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Orbit Correction in Particle Accelerators
Experiment: Integrate a reinforcement learning framework (e.g., DDPG or PPO) to train an agent using the MAD-X simulation as the environment. The agent's actions will correspond to adjustments in the 36 corrector magnets. Implement reward functions based on orbit deviations and penalties for exceeding current limits. Compare the RL-based approach's performance and adaptability to traditional methods under varying hidden parameter scenarios.

Name: predictive_control_with_lstm
Title: Predictive Control in Orbit Correction Using LSTM-Based Forecasting
Experiment: Develop a time-series forecasting model using LSTMs to predict future beam positions based on historical BPM data. Integrate this forecasting capability to preemptively adjust the corrector magnets before significant orbit deviations occur. Clearly define the interface between LSTM predictions and the existing correction framework. Evaluate the performance improvement in terms of reduced orbit correction frequency and enhanced stability under varying hidden parameter conditions.

Name: genetic_algorithm_orbit_optimization
Title: Genetic Algorithm for Optimizing Orbit Correction in VEPP-5
Experiment: Implement a genetic algorithm to optimize the settings of 36 corrector magnets in the VEPP-5 accelerator. Utilize the existing simulation framework to evaluate orbit deviations for different GA-generated configurations. Incorporate processes such as selection, crossover, and mutation to iteratively improve the solution. Compare performance metrics, such as L2 norm of orbit deviations and computation time, with existing methods like SVD and neural networks.

Name: interpretability_in_ai_orbit_correction
Title: Enhancing Interpretability in AI-Driven Orbit Correction for VEPP-5
Experiment: Integrate interpretability techniques such as SHAP or LIME into the neural network-based orbit correction framework. Implement a mechanism to visualize and analyze the importance of input features (BPM readings) in determining magnet settings. Evaluate the insights gained in terms of feature importance, model behavior, and potential biases. Use these insights to refine the model by improving training datasets or feature engineering strategies. Compare the interpretability results with traditional SVD methods to identify differences in decision-making processes.
